en.title: Tie-Break Protocols: Qualification and Shoot-Offs
en.excerpt: Official rules for breaking ties in qualification leaderboards (total 10s and Xs) and managing sudden-death one-arrow shoot-offs in elimination matches.
en.content:
Qualification Tie-Break Order

When two or more archers finish the qualification round with identical total scores, Archeris automatically resolves ties using official World Archery tie-break hierarchy:

  1. Total 10s Count: Total number of arrows scoring 10 (including inner-10 Xs).
  2. Total Xs Count: Total number of inner-ring X scores.
  3. Coin Toss / Shoot-off: If still tied for the final cut-off position entering the elimination bracket.

Individual One-Arrow Shoot-Off

If an elimination match is tied (5-5 set points for Recurve or equal total score for Compound):

  • Each archer shoots one arrow within 40 seconds.
  • The archer with the higher arrow value wins the match.

Closest to Center Measurement

If both archers shoot the exact same score (e.g., both shoot a 9 or both shoot a 10):

  • The arrow located closest to the center pinhole of the target wins.
  • The line judge measures the distance using an official caliper or measurement ruler.
  • In the scorekeeper app, check the Closest to Center toggle to designate the winner.

Team & Mixed Team Shoot-Offs

In team events, each member shoots one arrow (3 arrows for team, 2 arrows for mixed team). If total scores remain tied, the single arrow closest to the center determines the winning team.
